newsitem.title: INDIA: New Indian gold import rule effective Jan 1.
newsitem.headline: New Indian gold import rule effective Jan 1.

text.p: The Indian government said on Wednesday that the easing of a gold import restriction announced earlier this week would be effective from New Year's Day and the customs duty remained unchanged.
"The enhancement limit of 10 kg (22 lbs) up to which gold can be imported by passengers would come into force from 1st January, 1997," a Finance Ministry statement said.

On Tuesday, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said the government had allowed non-resident Indians to import 10 kg of gold every six months compared to five kg previously. The news agency did not say when the change would take effect.
The ministry said the rate of customs duty would remain unchanged at 220 rupees ($6.13) per 10 grams (0.35 oz).
PTI had quoted Finance Minister P. Chidambaram as saying the easing of the import rules would curb smuggling, shore up gold reserves and increase revenue from import duties.
India lifted a ban on gold imports in 1992 and has gradually liberalised trade in gold.
